questions.prompt: 6. Parent Alpha is preparing consolidated financial statements for 2023. On 1 January 2022, it purchased 49% of Company Beta for MCHF 350, including hidden reserves of MCHF 50 with a useful life of five years. Beta made MCHF 23 profit at the end of 2023. Which statements about Parent Alpha’s financial statement preparation are correct?
assumptions: IFRS; 49% gives significant influence without control. MCHF 50 is the total depreciable uplift. No tax effects; straight-line depreciation over five years begins at acquisition. Option b refers to the cumulative effect carried into 2023.

options.text: On 1 January 2022, Parent Alpha recognized an investment at the initial purchase price of MCHF 325.5 (350 minus its portion of hidden reserves).

options.explanation: Correct answer. The 49% share of the MCHF 50 hidden reserves is MCHF 24.5, depreciated at MCHF 4.9 a year, so the 2022 charge of MCHF 4.9 stays in the carrying amount carried into 2023.

options.text: Given the stake bought in Beta, Parent Alpha will fully consolidate Beta.
options.explanation: Wrong: 49% gives significant influence without control, so the equity method applies rather than full consolidation.

options.text: None of the above answers are correct.
options.explanation: Wrong: option b is correct, so 'none of the above' cannot be right.

questions.scenario:
Stuart’s Glasfabrik manufactures flower vases. The material for one vase costs CHF 1 and the glassblowers are paid wages of CHF 28 per hour. A glassblower can manufacture 10 vases per hour.

Fixed manufacturing costs amount to CHF 28’000 this year. Further costs that are not assigned to manufacturing amount to CHF 10’000 this year and are also fixed.
assumptions: Use the course linear CVP model within the relevant range: unchanged unit variable cost and total fixed cost, production equals sales, and no inventory changes.

options.explanation: Overstates production labor at 16,000 instead of 500 hours × CHF 28 = 14,000, so 5,000 + 16,000 + 28,000 = 49,000.
Adds the 10,000 non-manufacturing cost and another 14,000 of labor to 47,000, which counts labor twice and includes a cost outside manufacturing.
Correct answer. COGM = 5,000 × CHF 1 material + 500 hours × CHF 28 labor (CHF 14,000) + CHF 28,000 fixed manufacturing cost = CHF 47,000; the CHF 10,000 non-manufacturing cost is left out.
Overstates production labor at 31,000 instead of 14,000 (500 hours × CHF 28), so 5,000 + 31,000 + 28,000 = 64,000.

options.text: None of the answers A)–D) is correct.

- C) CHF 47’000
- D) CHF 64’000
- E) None of the answers A)–D) is correct.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true of cost and pricing decisions?

options.text: Companies only earn profits from selling products if they determine the prices.
options.explanation: Wrong: a company earns profit from sales when price exceeds unit cost on the volume it sells, not only because it sets the price.

options.text: Companies supply products as long as the price the customer is willing to pay for the products exceeds the incremental cost.
options.explanation: Accurate: a product is supplied while the customer's price exceeds the incremental cost. No option is keyed as correct; see note.

options.text: Companies supply products as long as there is demand for the product in the market, regardless of whether the price covers the incremental cost.
options.explanation: Wrong: a price below incremental cost loses money on each unit, so market demand alone does not justify supply.

questions.prompt:
After conducting a market research study, Doze Corp. decided to produce new wireless headphones to complement its standard headphone line. It is estimated that the new wireless headphones can be sold at a target price of CHF 240. The annual target sales volume for wireless headphones is 21’000 units. What is the target cost?
assumptions: Target cost means total annual cost, not cost per unit.

options.explanation: Equals target revenue (240 × 21,000 = 5,040,000) and ignores the 20% target operating income.
Gives 1,008,000, which is the target operating income (20% of 5,040,000), not the target cost.
Adds the 20% margin to revenue (5,040,000 × 1.2) instead of subtracting it.
Correct answer. Target cost = target price × volume × (1 − 20%) = 240 × 21,000 × 0.80 = CHF 4,032,000, or CHF 192 per unit.

options.text: None of the answers A)–D) is correct.

questions.explanation: Target cost equals revenue less target operating profit. A margin on sales uses revenue as its base.

questions.prompt: At what amount does Halvora initially recognize the lease liability on 1 January 2025?
questions.scenario: On 1 January 2025, Halvora AG leases a packaging line from Krenn Leasing AG. The lease runs four years, which equals the line’s useful life. Halvora pays CHF 6,200 at the end of each year (31 December). The interest rate implicit in the lease is 7%. Halvora reports under IFRS and depreciates right-of-use assets straight-line.
assumptions: IFRS 16 lessee; no residual value, purchase option, initial direct costs or incentives. Round interest and balances to cents; round the requested final amount up to the next franc.

options.explanation: Correct answer. Discounting four payments of CHF 6,200 at 7% gives CHF 21,000.71, which rounds up to CHF 21,001.
Adds the four payments without discounting. The liability is a present value, so the time value of money is missing.
Discounts the total of all payments by one year only. Each payment has to be discounted for its own year.
Treats the payments as due in advance (annuity due). Halvora pays at year-end, so each payment is discounted one more year.

questions.explanation: The lease liability equals the present value of the outstanding lease payments, discounted at the implicit rate.

options.explanation: This is the 2025 interest. In 2026 interest is charged on the lower balance left after the first payment.
Correct answer. Opening 2026 liability CHF 16,270.76 × 7% = CHF 1,138.95, rounded up to CHF 1,139.
This is the principal part of the 2026 payment, not the interest part.
Adds two years of interest on the original liability. Interest is charged each year on the balance still outstanding.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Halvora’s lease is correct under IFRS 16?
questions.scenario: On 1 January 2025, Halvora AG leases a packaging line from Krenn Leasing AG. The lease runs four years, which equals the line’s useful life. options.text: The lease payments are recognized as rental expense; no asset or liability appears on the balance sheet.
options.explanation: That was operating-lease treatment before IFRS 16. A lessee now recognizes a right-of-use asset and a lease liability.

options.text: Krenn Leasing AG, the lessor, recognizes the right-of-use asset.

questions.prompt: Which deferred tax balance does Morvik report for the machine on 31 December 2025?

options.explanation: Correct answer. Book value CHF 14,400,000 exceeds the tax base CHF 10,800,000 by CHF 3,600,000; × 21% = CHF 756,000.
The amount is right but the direction is reversed. Book value above tax base means more tax later, so it is a liability.
This is the temporary difference before applying the 21% tax rate.

Zentra Logistik AG bought a refrigerated truck on 1 January 2023 for CHF 420,000. It is depreciated straight-line over seven years with no residual value. At 31 December 2025, after a new emissions rule, Zentra tests the truck for impairment:

| Item | CHF |
|---|---:|
| Value in use | 205,000 |
| Fair value | 228,000 |
| Costs of disposal | 12,000 |

options.explanation: Compares with value in use only. Fair value less costs of disposal (CHF 216,000) is higher and sets the recoverable amount.
Ignores the CHF 12,000 costs of disposal when measuring fair value less costs of disposal.
Correct answer. Carrying amount 240,000; recoverable amount = max(205,000; 216,000) = 216,000; loss = CHF 24,000.
The carrying amount of CHF 240,000 exceeds both recoverable measures, so a loss is required.

questions.explanation: Recoverable amount is the higher of value in use and fair value less costs of disposal. The loss is carrying amount minus recoverable amount.
